newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gap in October Brent blurs crystal balls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gap in October Brent blurs crystal balls.

text.p: Technical analysts were divided over the near-term trend of IPE October Brent futures after prices gapped lower on Tuesday, settled near the session low and were nearing important support at $20 and $19.87 a barrel.
"I would be bullish at this point. I think we've done our downside move already," said Mark Power at MMS International in Tokyo. "I would be advising people to liquidate shorts and initiate longs."
"Usually when we have a gap lower the market usually fills the gap and that would be supportive for a move higher."
Hourly fast stochastics have reached oversold levels near 15 percent, suggesting an upside correction was probable even if there is follow through selling right at the open, he said.

He put support levels at the psychological $20 level, which is also a Fibonacci retracement to October's rally from $18.34 on July 29 to its contract high of $20.98 on August 19, and then at $19.90. He also sees significant support at $19.50.

"We've just completed a downside retracement to $20 and I think we'll start an impulsive move up to $21.54, which is a 61.8 percent projection of the move from $16.50 on May 20 to $19.62," Power said.

But Ken Seehusen, editor of Chart Insight in Cedar Falls, Iowa, drew bearish implications from the gap which he said could drag prices in the next few sessions to as low as $19.62, the high in the month of July.

"Closes below last week's reaction low of $20.16 would confirm (Tuesday's) gap was a downside breakaway gap," he said. "If (Tuesday's) gap is maintained, look for a pausible pause or retest of the gap on Wednesday. However, markets in an uptrend should not gap lower if the underlying tone of the market is still strong."
Oct Brent closed Tuesday at $20.03 and left a small gap on its daily chart from $20.37 to its Friday low of $20.40.

The sharply lower open Tuesday, which was tracking the losses in New York on Monday when the IPE was closed, also violated a minor uptrend line dating to the August 16 low of $19.87. A longer-term trendline from the late July lows held on Tuesday but crosses today near $20.05-$20.10.
Oct Brent was expected to open Wednesday down 5-10 cents.
"Bearish divergence by stochastics have been warning bulls at least a corrective break was needed," Seehusen said.
He added that further weakness today would turn the daily ADX, a trend indicator, down, signalling "the market has lost its upside momentum and a near-term trend change is taking place."
